title: MV Cowboy Kyle and the Realm of Fables

posts.author: P1XELFACE
posts.body:
Welcome to the Realm of Fables, where every day is an adventure and every lifetime is a story to echo across the ages.  This tale follows the exploits of the infamous bandits, Cowboy Kyle and Lil Root.  Arriving in the wild West Arcadia, they seek to enrich themselves on gold.
However a chance encounter with (and attempted scam on) Diane, the daughter of the West Arcadian Mining Co.'s founder, will derail their story and send them on a trio of epic adventures.
The current version of the game is a single screen arcade game.  However I have some large plans for the future of the project, turning it into a collection of games!  Each one will have different gameplay styles, such as a rogue-like or an exploration heavy action rpg, and continue the story set up in the original game.  I might even make a few more arcade games for the collection, since I just enjoy doing that.
The game can be played with one or two players, keyboard and gamepad are both supported.  Whatever you use to start a game from the title screen decides Player 1's input.  On the character select screen, Player 2 just has to press one of the designated buttons to be assigned their controller.
EXPANDED STORY
Spoiler
Cowboy Kyle and Lil Root are a couple of adventuring outlaws who come to the land of West Arcadia looking for their next big score.  Fresh off of robbing another outlaw, the infamous Wild Wilbur, Kyle was spending his last gold coin at the saloon when he spotted Diane, the heiress of the West Arcadian Mining Co.  Her father is known to be a foppish and clumsy man, often dropping entire sacks of gold and an awful idea pops into his head...
He dashes across the counter, nearly launching Diane's friends, and puts on the old Cowboy Kyle charm with his signature catchphrase, "Howdy Parder".  Instantly charming the young woman.  Now "dating" and able to stay close to Diane's father, Kyle brings his best friend Lil Root to join in scooping up the dropped money bags.  However, Diane's friends, three witches know better and seek to stop the "heroes" from finishing their dastardly scheme, while Wild Wilbur has finally caught wind of their location and seeks to claim his revenge on them.
Though elsewhere in the world, catastrophic events are starting to unfold...
A vampire king with a twisted sense of morality is about to hear about the "worst" possible news about West Arcadia and in the darkest depths of the demon-realm, a massive and terrible army is forming to strike the Celestial-realm and upset the balance of life itself.
CHARACTERS
Spoiler
The infamous gunslinger known for his dashing smile on wanted posters and his signature catchphrase, the poorly spelled “HOWDY PARDER”.  Grew up an orphan and practically raised on dime novels about cowboys, he ran away to the West Arcadian frontier. There his raw talent caught the attention of the legendary Nameless One, where he was trained alongside the man’s finest apprentices.  Whatever destiny the Nameless One has in store for Kyle, the cowboy doesn’t dwell on the details, instead concerned with securing his favorite thing in the world, beans.
Kyle’s love of beans borders on cult-like devotions and is actually the driving force behind everything he does.  If he has to fight three endlessly respawning witches, a country full of monsters or an entire demon army for a single can of the stuff, he will.  He’s never told anyone why this is, for he is a man of few words preferring to let his partner, Lil Root do the talking since they’re usually on the same page and he prefers the sound of her voice over his own.  If he needs to give some words, a tip of his hat or a “HOWDY PARDER” is all he needs.
Lil Root is a former Wakanari warrior who abandoned her responsibilities to pursue what she believes to be her true calling, seeing the world and drinking as much root beer as possible.  The once celebrated hero who would wrestle a bear to protect children found new glory as an infamous outlaw, always bouncing from one ill conceived scheme to the next.
Hyperactive and a bit unhinged, Lil Root found a life long companion is Kyle, the only person that could match her in a fight.  Her love for root beer fuels every one of her terrible ideas and her mighty battle cry.  Where Kyle is quiet and immovable, Lil Root is loud, fast and endlessly animated, and together make a shakable duo bonded by their love of adventure, mayhem, and a good meal by the camp fire.
Diane is the heiress of the West Arcadian Gold Company, raised in wealth but taught to use it for the good of others by her father.  Now, she’s a sharp, observant business woman with an uncanny ability to read people, and very talented at playing the fool to lure unsuspecting scoundrels into a world of hurt.
While she recognizes the evil of greedy people who already have everything, her naivety shines when faced with the evil of desperation driven greed of those who have nothing, a lesson she’ll have to learn about some day.  Until then, she’ll do her best to better her community and the lives of those in the company, being a good friend to them and travelers like the witches.
Known only as Father, the founder and head of the West Arcadian Gold Company and the widowed parent of Diane.  He’s a genuinely generous man who takes only what he needs fairly and makes sure to use his power for the betterment of the world, finding his calling 15 years ago forming an alliance with the Wakanari tribe to chase out Greedly Gains inc. and stopping their ambition to chase away the locals and strip mine the earth.
Despite his good intentions, Father can be absent minded and clumsy, frequently tripping on nothing and landing flat on his back and dropping large money bags he meant to deliver to the people of the town, making him an easy target for thieves.  His soft exterior does hide the heart of a warrior, and anyone who harms his precious daughter or dares compare him to the vile Gregory Greedly will soon find out about.
Beth is a witch from Vampire Land who runs the Brunhilda Potion Shop.  As the middle sister of her coven, Beth has made peace with living a fairly mundane life by witch standards, running her shop, doting on Maple too much and often bickering with Claudia, with occasional trips over to West Arcadia.
However she has found a love for the cowboy lifestyle, modeling her spell slinging techniques after them, and while a bit slow on the draw, she remains nimble on her feet.  Secretly, she admires Cowboy Kyle and wishes she could get away living like he does.
Claudia is the matriarch of the Brunhilda coven and an ancient fossil of days long past.  She is very old and very ugly, and takes both facts with pride, having a cackle that can curdle milk and a love of adding newt’s foot and fish eyes to her potions for flavor.
Now, she’s sharp tongued and wickedly critical, especially towards Maple’s laziness, but deep… DEEP down in her blackened heart remains that of her old title, Claudia the Kind, the Champion of Vampire Land.
Maple is the youngest of the Brunhilda coven and a former student and drop out of Saint Toadmire's Academy for Gifted Creeps.  While she neglected traditional magic studies, she excelled with alarming enthusiasm in Slashing and Stabbing 101.
These days she works part time at the Brunhilda Potion Shop to pay her rent, putting in just the right amount of effort to keep on Beth’s good side, despite Claudia’s protest.  Sometimes however, she thinks about her ex-boyfriend, the now king Batula, and wonders what could have been.
Sherri is one of the West Arcadian Gold Company’s founding members and its resident demolition man and bomb maker, channeling her unbridled hatred for rocks into her work passionately.  She’ll never be pleased with her results however, as she always survives her own explosions.  She might be a bit crazy.
Despite her quirks, Sherry is a good friend to her fellow miners, Diane and the citizens of the town, and if you need something destroyed, she’ll happily enlist herself for the job.
Pierre is a raven from East Arcadia and a founding member of the West Arcadia Gold Company and its quiet, awkward but ever polite gadgeteer.  He spends most of his time hunched over half finished projects and looking for excuses to upgrade any gear he can get his hands on, something Kyle and Lil Root provide in spades.
He doesn’t talk about himself or his past, and those that have known him from the beginning understand why, but sometimes when he spots a Greedly Gains Inc. logo, you can feel a history between them.
Storm Boy is an old friend of Father Hartstone and Claudia's, founding member and co-owner of the West Arcadian Gold Company.  Across West Arcadia he's a well respected gentleman and often called in to oversee construction or demolition projects, when he's not managing contracting jobs for the company, and acts as an honorary uncle towards Diane, Pierre and Sherri... few would think there was a time he was a disgrace Wakanari warrior living in exile.
Now a days, he mostly likes to hang out in the saloon, gambling in his favorite game, Undertaker.  Few have the guts to play against him, not because he's really good, but because he's rather infamous for being a sore loser.  If you befriend Father, it's only a matter of time before you're sitting across the table from him, try to stay on his good side.
Richard Buckhorn is the local lawman of West Arcadia and widely celebrated for capturing some of the most infamous outlaws in the region… despite the inconvenient truth that he always arrives after the fighting is over.  Lazy, dim and profoundly unmotivated, Buckhorn spends most of his days asleep at his desk or nursing a mug of root beer, always confused when people praise him or give him medals.
Despite appearances, he isn’t malicious, greedy or even egotistical, just incredibly incompetent and content to go along with whatever’s happening, be it a boring day or participating in a parade in his honor.
Pocho is a chicken and the loyal deputy under Sheriff Buckhorn.  Unlike his boss, Poncho is actually competent, with a sharp eye and quick reflexes and armed with his preferred weapon, his wife.  Together, they fire explosive eggs at their enemies, and neither find anything unusual about the arrangement.
Pocho believes the legends surrounding Buckhorn completely and without question, charging into danger under the belief that together, justice shall prevail.
Trixie's a member of the Noctara, a race of humanoids with bat like wings that can fold into usable arms, and she's come to West Arcadia for two reasons, to peddle her collection of probably not cursed trinkets and to bother a certain dorky raven.
She can be sassy, flirty, and a bit morbid, but she's honest and values connections with people more than anything, even if she's not one to stay in a single place too long.  If you see the faint green glow of her lantern, come on down to her wagon and see what she has in store for you.
The Goddess of Gold and Queen of the Celestial Realm, a radiant kingdom of floating islands suspended far above the mortal world.  As her divine responsibility, she oversees the cycle of gold between the divine and moral realms, keeping the balance of life on a steady path forward always.
For her, gods are bound by duty and fate, something mortals naturally rebel against, and in a cast of weirdos she sticks out as the only normal one.  Despite that, she deeply values her friendship with the Nameless One, her former champion she misses dearly.
Jack is a werewolf and proud member of the Wild Rodeo, a villainous band of outlaws led by the enigmatic and unhinged Wild Wilbur.  While the  Rodeo seeks to bring total anarchy to the world, Jack treats it as just a job to support his wife and 9 kids.
On the job, he fights like a rabid dog lunging and biting everything in sight, often literally chewing the scenery.  Off the clock, he’s a wonderful husband and father to his family.  Like a true werewolf, he’s a man of two very different lives.
Fredrick Nicholas Solar is a cyclops from the southern territory of the Amazonia Wildlands and the Wild Rodeo’s chief engineer.  No matter how absurd, impractical or down right dangerous a contraption Wil Wilbur dreams up, he’ll be able to make it real.
Contrasting his brilliance and imposing figure, Solar’s actually a total coward, easily pushed around by his cohorts especially by Queen Cobra.  Regardless, if forced into battle, he’ll pilot his custom one man tank and roll into combat, praying he survives.
Nefertiti Cobra is a former ruler of the Starbound Desert, dead for five thousand years before the gold rush revived her mummified body and reignited her ambitions.  Desiring gold more than her old throne, she booked it to West Arcadia with the desire to decorate herself in as much of it as possible.
Vain and greedy, yet irresistibly charming, Cobra joined the Wild Rodeo and immediately decided she was in charge (she's not), becoming incredibly bossy towards her fellow outlaws, and shooting out super sonic screeches and extending her neck to bite down on anyone foolish enough to defy the queen.
Orobus, the feared general of the demon clan leads the invasion of the Celestial Realm under the orders of her beloved master, Malnar.  As a Gold Succubus, she feeds not on souls or… other less than child friendly things, but instead she eats gold like we eat beans or root beer.  She’s devoted to the cause and believes in her demonic brethren, often serving as the hype man to them for every battle.
She can channel the gold in her stomach into glimmering fireballs and mimic the powers of others by donning enchanted golden clothes resembling them.  She’s also a self proclaimed master of disguise, but if her crimson skin or gold plated horns don’t give her away, her signature laugh, “HEK HECK HECK HECK!” will…
The current king of Vampire Land is a neurotic weirdo with an inverted moral compass where good is bad and bad is good, and he’s gonna do all the “good” he can and expect you to thank him for it.  His misguided attempts to help has turned him into a mediocre ruler, but sometimes his best friend and butler, Edgar Rottingham can convince him to go against his morals and do some “wrong” for a change.
He’s the former class clown of Saint Toadmire’s Academy for Gifted Creeps and the ex-boyfriend of Maple Brunhilda, but keeps an amicable relationship with the witch now.  He has a strange respect for Cowboy Kyle, Lil Root, Sherry Bomb, and even the Wild Rodeo, praising them as “the only people around here with some class in that back water dump West Arcadia.”
WILD WILBUR
Wild Wilbur is the leader of the Wild Rodeo and a man with a simple goal, total world wide anarchy.  No one knows his backstory, and if asked Wilbur will tell you it’s far too mundane to be worth tellin’.  His only interest in gold is simply to fund his crazy contraptions and keep his gang fed, caring more about causing chaos and the spectacle of his insanity, but his focus has recently shifted to revenge on Cowboy Kyle and Lil Root for robbing him just weeks ago.
He is utterly insane and willing to throw himself and his entire army into impossible situations even for the slightest chance of settling the score.  His presence alone can unsettle the most hardened of outlaws, monsters and even demons.  Amongst the divine, his name is spoken in hushed tones, a demon to the demons and a look in his eyes able to petrify a gorgon.  He isn’t super natural, just the worst combination of crazy, dedicated, and having the muscle to back it up.
OUTLAW OAFS
A collective of failed gunslingers, men and women who were simply too slow, too stupid, or too predictable to amount to anything as a cowboy.  Meant to be cast aside as background filler and forgotten by history, Wild Wilbur gave them a new purpose under his banner and a lust for revenge against the very narrative that told them “you don’t matter”.
Wilbur is surprisingly a pretty good boss, he’d be perfect if not for him expecting them to join him on whatever insane plan he has, but they won’t hesitate to charge into battle and fight alongside their boss.  They prove with enough idiocy and backbone, even the worthless has-beens who never were can become a force audacious enough to shake the heavens.
Perhaps out of respect for their boss, some have taken up new talents, like handling long range rifles, teleportation, jumping high, and some were even the failed apprentices of the Nameless One, flawed mostly in their inability to watch their backs.
DEAD EYE OAFS
These are the most elite members of the Wild Rodeo’s grunts, made up of the Nameless One’s slain rivals who have returned from Hell for revenge.  Denies their true target, they’ve settled for revenge by proxy against Cowboy Kyle, and Wild Wilbur seems to always be on his tail.
They do not talk, sleep or eat, and when not deployed they simply stand in place waiting for orders in dead silence.  They unsettle anyone who isn’t Wilbur, who treats them like any other henchman.  Like the Outlaw Oafs they are slow on their feet, but not out of incompetence, but instead patience.  Every step is carefully measured, every angle they’re ready to fire instantly, methodically minded, patient and extremely dangerous, they know it’s only a matter of time before their target messes up.

posts.author: P1XELFACE
posts.body:
Hello everyone, I just wanted to announce Version 0.12 is out now, it's focused on fixing some issues in the game with a few new features.
Bug Fixes:
Both players choosing the same character and color no longer glitches the game, and everything should load fine now.  (This affected single player as the player 2 character still shows up in the game over screen).
Player 2's life count doesn't set to 1 in the Viejo Corazon stage anymore.  This was an oversight from testing the time out feature.
New Features:
The witches and Wild Wilbur have new and more colorful sprites now.  You can set the witches to use their old sprites in the Options screen if you want.
New Options, Deadly Friendly Fire, which causes friendly fire to KO the other player, and Random Respawn, which switches your character and color every time you die.
Options screen is now accessible from the Character Select screen.
The Tutorial is now much easier to skip, prompting you on the initial loading screen and letting you decline all together.
Download links are in the main post up top.

posts.author: P1XELFACE
posts.body:
The game is finally listed on Itch, and hopefully we'll be seeing no more issues with it.
Version 0.2 is developing well, Beth and Claudia are fully playable and I will be working on Maple soon. Furthermore I'll be testing out some mild rogue-lite elements for the 1st game allowing you to collect cash and upgrade your characters, and when I'm done updating the core game I'm hoping to have the versus mode done in a day.
With versus mode in mind everyone will be playing differently and Cowboy Kyle and Lil Root will also be diverging stat wise:
Kyle becoming stronger and slightly faster, making him better at fighting tanky enemies.
Lil Root having a much better Special economy, making her better at dodging and positioning.
Beth will reward high skill play, being mediocre until she uses her power up special and automatically renews itself if played optimally.
Claudia will have slower projectile allowing for trickier shots and her teleport gives her unmatched movement but requires strict attention to her special meter.
Maple might change between now and release, but she's planned to be a very mobile character with a fast but short ranged attack and able to jump between floors without a ladder.
The Cowboy Kyle 2 demo will probably take me at least a week or two to put together, requiring new tilesets, enemies, and several more subtle gameplay changes.
The tutorial is being completely overhauled as an optional mode, but still recommended on first time booting up the game.  The new one will be more like a mini playground that lets you learn the mechanics of each character, obstacles patterns, and item functionality in a safe, controlled space and at your own pace.  Cutscenes within the tutorial will still be in the game, just accessed differently now.
I regret to say this but old save files will not be valid in the next release.  It's come to my attention an issue with Chrono Engine is if you add tools (attacks) to the game and load an old save file, it just won't acknowledge the new tools.
I'm taking some precautions to get around this in future releases, but for version 0.2 exclusively I'll allow you to input your old high score on first boot up of the game, so I'll trust you to be honest here.
I thank you all for your support so far, and hope you are satisfied with version 0.2 and later updates to the project!
